summary: A 1970 status report on the Network Control Program at UCSB and RAND, by three authors.

plainLanguage.summary: UCSB and RAND tested their Network Control Programs by exchanging console information. Both NCPs behaved according to the protocol, while RAND identified minor issues in the program that interfaced graphics consoles with its NCP.

subtitle: Results of console-to-console NCP testing between UCSB and RAND.

tldr.problem: UCSB and RAND needed to check whether their Network Control Programs behaved according to Document #1.
tldr.mechanism: The sites tested their NCPs by connecting UCSB and RAND consoles to each other.
tldr.outcome: Both NCPs responded as specified; RAND found minor issues in its Network Services Program interface involving data conversion and status display.

sections.title: NCP Checkout
sections.content: UCSB and RAND conducted console-to-console validation of their Network Control Programs. The exercise was intended to verify that the NCPs behaved according to Document #1 protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The two sites connected their consoles through their NCPs to check protocol behavior. The report describes this as a validation exercise.

sections.title: What the Test Found
sections.content:
The report says the UCSB and RAND NCPs responded as specified in Document #1. RAND found a few minor problems in its Network Services Program, which interfaces video graphics consoles to the NCP.

The problems concerned data-format conversions and human factors in the presentation of status information on displays.
sections.plainLanguage: The NCPs followed the specified behavior. The issues RAND found concerned data conversion and how status information appeared on the console.

sections.title: Planned Follow-Up
sections.content: UCSB and RAND offered to participate in validation exercises with other sites. They planned further exercises involving data reconfigurations and file transmissions.
sections.plainLanguage: The sites offered to test with others and planned to examine data reconfiguration and file transfer next.
